title: Extract weight-format transpiler and streamline tokenizer bridge
creator: Aisha Choudhury
description:
Background: Over the last 18 months we've accumulated a set of ad-hoc weight format adapters (legacy .ckpt variants, two homegrown manifest styles, and a polyglot loader used only for a short-lived partner experiment). These adapters live inside the model-loader process and bring multiple decoder paths, duplicated checksum/validation logic, and a tight coupling between tokenizer initialization and weight activation. Consequences: slower cold-model load times, sporadic memory pressure spikes during format detection, and brittle tokenizer handshakes that require per-format special casing.

Goal: Extract a small, well-documented 'weight-format transpiler' component that converts legacy formats into a single canonical manifest consumed by the runtime, and replace the current in-process tokenizer handoff with a small async 'tokenizer bridge' interface (IDL + lightweight shim) to decouple tokenizer lifecycle from weight activation. The combined changes should: reduce model load tail latency by >=20%, remove duplicated validation code, enable incremental dependency upgrades (numpy/pillow/serialization libs) inside the transpiler, and make format migrations observable via logs/metrics.

Scope: The ticket covers design, a prototype transpiler service (runs as a short-lived CLI or sidecar), a tokenizer bridge spec with two reference shims (CPython and Rust-core bridge), updates to the model registry ingestion path to emit canonical manifests, and an integration demo for two representative models (one large multishard and one small single-file). Not included: migrating every existing third-party adapter (that will be follow-ups).

Out-of-scope risks/constraints: retention of backward compatibility for existing deployments until cutover, no changes to external API surface, must not increase peak memory for steady-state inference.

Design notes and tradeoffs: We considered embedding a single heavyweight converter in the loader but rejected it due to repeated memory allocations and longer GC pauses. The transpiler-as-service allows dependency isolation (we can upgrade libs inside the transpiler without affecting the runtime), and produces a cached canonical manifest plus checksums. The tokenizer bridge uses a minimal async handshake: register(model_manifest_id) -> preload(vocab_prefixes) -> ready. This avoids blocking weight streaming on tokenizer I/O.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical manifest produced for both test models and consumed by runtime without format-specific branches
Model cold-start median load latency reduced by >=20% in benchmark harness for multishard test case
No duplicated checksum logic remains in runtime; single validation path used
Tokenizer bridge handshake implemented and validated by integration test (CPython shim)
Transpiler runs as standalone CLI/sidecar and has a basic logging/metrics surface (success/fail/counts/latency)
Migration plan documented with rollback steps and a small data-migration script
Two GitHub PRs opened: transpiler prototype and tokenizer bridge spec; CI green and perf benchmarks attached

Design canonical manifest schema and document in confluence (link below)
Implement transpiler prototype as isolated Python package with its own virtualenv and CI
Add runtime consumer that reads canonical manifest and removes format-detection branches
Define tokenizer bridge IDL and implement CPython shim that can be used in tests
Run perf regressions and memory profiling across representative models
Prepare migration plan and a small tool to convert cached artifacts in S3
Coordinate cutover with infra and monitoring teams; add observability dashboards
